Priya to share SOC 2 + ISO artifacts and KMS/HSM architecture diagram by 2027-10-05
Customer to confirm target SLA and signoff owners by 2027-10-10

action_items: Owner: Jordan Lee; Item: Email redlined MSA and proposed SLA terms; Due: 2027-10-07
Owner: Priya Natarajan; Item: Upload security pack (SOC2, ISO, penetration test summary) and KMS diagram; Due: 2027-10-05
Owner: Elysian - Maya Thompson; Item: Provide procurement timeline and legal approver contact; Due: 2027-10-10

summary: Procurement and legal review between Redwood AE/SE and Elysian Health procurement/legal/security. Main topics: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA uptime and latency SLOs, KMS/HSM and encryption at rest/transit, dedicated vs hosted deployment, pricing approval for a 30-day pilot. Agreed next steps include sending redlines, sharing security artifacts, and provisioning a pilot environment for security and perf verification.
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I see Maya, Alan, Samir, Rita from Elysian, and Priya and Luis from Redwood. Uh, we planned 45 minutes to run through the MSA/DPA and SLAs
are we good?
00:08 Maya Thompson: Yes, thanks. We're mainly here to get the legal redline items clarified and understand the SLAs for a clinical workload. Procurement timeline is tight so we want to move quick.
00:18 Samir Patel: Quick note from legal side: we have standard redlines on data processing, liability caps, and audit rights. Also need to confirm data residency and encryption with KMS.

00:30 Priya Natarajan: Great, I'll address the technical parts. High level, Redwood supports hosted API and dedicated pools. For regulated workloads we usually recommend Dedicated or Private with VPC and customer-managed KMS. There's a tradeoff in latency and cost between hosted and dedicated though.

00:45 Dr. Alan Ruiz: For us latency matters for inference in clinician workflows 
 sub-500ms p50 ideally for short prompts. Can you speak to latency SLOs and how you measure them?

00:55 Priya Natarajan: Sure. On hosted our published p50/p95 numbers vary by model; for a dedicated pool we can guarantee lower variance because of isolated capacity. Our SLA typically covers uptime 
 e.g., 99.9% 
 but we can discuss latency SLOs as an operational metric in the runbook. Note: we do auto-bursting to avoid throttles but that affects pricing.
01:12 Maya Thompson: On the MSA we have a clause wanting SOC 2 plus penetration test summary. Do you provide those?
01:18 Jordan Lee: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and an ISO attestation; Priya will share the security pack. We'll also provide a recent pen test summary. I'll send links after the call.
01:28 Rita Huang: For encryption - we need customer-managed keys. Can your Private/VPC option integrate with our KMS or HSM?

01:36 Priya Natarajan: Yes, for Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM integration. For Dedicated we also support bringing-your-own-KMS for at-rest encryption; for hosted we have options for envelope encryption and limited BYOK for enterprise plans. There's sometimes a config lead time.

01:48 Samir Patel: Liability and indemnity 
 our legal wants to keep a standard cap tied to fees; you have a higher cap in your template. Can we negotiate closer to our standard?

01:56 Jordan Lee: Totally understand. We typically have tiers 
 enterprise customers can negotiate liability caps and specific indemnities. We'll propose adjusted language in the redline we send.

02:05 Dr. Alan Ruiz: Another technical question 
 how do you handle KV cache and session replay? We want assurance patient data is not cached beyond session retention policies.

02:14 Priya Natarajan: We have automatic KV/prefix caching optimizations, but for regulated data we can disable or isolate caching per-customer or route. We'll note that in the runbook and the DPA 
 retention settings are configurable.

02:30 Maya Thompson: About SLAs 
 we need a 99.95% uptime for core inference endpoints, and a financial credit mechanism. Is that possible?

02:40 Jordan Lee: We can propose an SLA schedule. 99.9% is our standard for hosted, but 99.95% can be scoped for Dedicated with committed capacity. Credits and remediation steps will be in the SLA appendix 
 we'll include proposed language in the redline package.

02:54 Priya Natarajan: Important to note that a latency SLO tied to credits is unusual; typically credits are for availability. For latency we provide monitoring, alerting, and runbook playbooks but recommend a pilot to validate p50/p95 on your workload.
03:08 Maya Thompson: Procurement needs pricing for the pilot. We need to know committed vs burst pricing, and if we go Dedicated what the minimum term is.

03:16 Luis Gomez: For Dedicated we have monthly reserved commits; burst is available with overage pricing. For pilots we often run a 30-day dedicated pilot with a temporary commit 
 we can send a pricing sheet. We'll include committed unit pricing and burst rates.

03:28 Samir Patel: DPA specifics 
 we require audit logs with exportability and retention controls. Do you provide per-request audit logs and access logs?

03:36 Priya Natarajan: Yes, per-request audit logs are available; for Private and Dedicated you can control retention. Hosted customers have configurable retention windows; for enterprise we can extend retention or provide log exports to your SIEM.
03:47 Dr. Alan Ruiz: Any regulators we should be aware of? We operate across US and EU so data residency matters.
03:54 Jordan Lee: We support regional deployments and can pin logs/data to regions. For EU data residency we recommend deploying to our EU region or Private deployment in your VPC.

04:04 Maya Thompson: Onboard checklist 
 we need: signed MSA/DPA, security artifacts, a run of a perf test, and vendor onboarding form completed by our procurement team. Can Redwood provide a single onboarding doc?
04:14 Luis Gomez: Yes, we'll provide a vendor onboarding packet with the technical contacts, runbook, and a checklist for procurement. I'll attach the packet to the email when we follow up.

04:26 Samir Patel: One more legal point: data breach notification SLA 
 we need 72 hours. Can you commit to that?
04:33 Jordan Lee: We commit to industry-standard notification windows; 72 hours is our default for security incidents. We'll include explicit language in the DPA.

04:42 Maya Thompson: Timeline 
 procurement committee meets next Wednesday, we need legal redlines by Monday EOD to make it. Is that feasible?

04:48 Jordan Lee: We'll prioritize and target Monday EOD for an initial redline package, and Priya will send security artifacts by Tuesday morning at the latest. Luis will follow up with pricing and pilot details by Wednesday.
05:00 Dr. Alan Ruiz: If we run pilot and performance looks good, what's typical lead time to go production on Dedicated?
05:08 Priya Natarajan: From pilot to production usually 2-6 weeks depending on procurement and network setup. Private on-prem can take longer due to air-gap installs and KMS integrations.
05:18 Maya Thompson: Any open items around certification? We might need ISO/ SOC attestation scans.

05:23 Priya Natarajan: We'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary right after. Also we can provide a pen test executive summary 
 details under NDA if requested.

05:34 Samir Patel: On pricing approvals: procurement needs an internal cost justification doc 
 can Redwood supply an expected TCO comparison for hosted vs dedicated vs private?

05:44 Jordan Lee: Yes, we can produce a short TCO analysis and include expected token/unit cost, estimated latency improvements, and projected savings from caching/quantization. We'll mark that as a deliverable.
05:58 Rita Huang: Are there any third-party subprocessors we use? We need a list for compliance review.
06:05 Priya Natarajan: We use cloud providers and some telemetry vendors; we'll include a subprocessors list in the security pack. If there's a showstopper, we can discuss contractual restrictions.
06:16 Maya Thompson: Okay, let's recap next steps...

06:19 Jordan Lee: Recap: Jordan sends redlined MSA/DPA and SLA appendix by 2027-10-07, Priya shares security artifacts and KMS diagram by 2027-10-05, Luis provisions a 30-day dedicated pilot and a pricing sheet by 2027-10-06, Elysian confirms procurement approvers by 2027-10-10. Any additions?
06:35 Maya Thompson: That covers it. We'll look out for the email and try to review quickly to hit Wednesday committee. Thanks all.
06:42 Jordan Lee: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the package. Bye.
45:00 [call ended]
